items.note: CHI system paper: InspirationGraph, a structured text-to-image tool for early product-design ideation, tested in a 24-person user study; the abstract does not name a comparison condition or say whether design outputs were scored, so it may be a system paper with no comparison (and is under 50 participants).

Pre-registered random-assignment experiments in which people practiced cover-letter writing with an AI tool versus alone, googling examples, or human editor feedback, then wrote cover letters without AI; outcome is writing quality rather than creativity (an after_ai design), so the next stage should check whether the task fits the creativity scope; sample sizes not given in the abstract.

Mostly a model study of data-augmented LLM research-idea generation (climate negotiation), plus a human study in which researchers proposed ideas with or without the LLM ideas and validation, and the assisted ideas were rated higher quality; sample size and assignment not stated.

Three-arm randomized experiment (900 randomized, 659 analyzed): self-generation-first AI workflow, direct-adoption AI workflow, or no AI for a first argumentative essay, then a parallel essay without AI; blind raters scored reasoning quality, idea diversity, and originality (after_ai, possibly also with_ai on the first essay).

Participants sketched abstract concepts before and after GPT-4 verbal or visual inspiration (AI configuration comparison plus a pre/post contrast); sketches scored by neural-network semantic distance and uniqueness and by human and GPT-4 creativity ratings; abstract found through OpenAlex under DOI 10.48448/wd46-dd26; sample size and assignment not stated (CogSci proceedings, likely small).

Quasi-experiment with 65 students in a design thinking course using a generative-AI-enhanced collaborative whiteboard versus a conventional platform; creativity and critical thinking measured with pre- and post-tests, which may be tests or questionnaires rather than scores on the design output.

Nature Communications system paper on iDesignGPT, an LLM multi-agent framework for conceptual engineering design; novelty and originality metrics are computed on system outputs versus LLM baselines, and two controlled user studies (search notes: n = 11 and n = 37) compare human-only design with LLM workflows but report mainly reception and mental demand; whether participants' designs were scored is unclear.

150 undergraduates wrote creatively under five collaboration conditions (human-human, human-computer or human-robot with a high- or low-creativity LLM); originality, imagery, voice, and semantic flow scored by experts and computational measures; allocation procedure not stated.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Crossref, Europe PMC empty; Semantic Scholar rate-limited); title and search snippets suggest an AIGC-based design method improved novelty and elaboration of student design outcomes, so classified as a possible experiment pending full text.

Evaluates Stable Diffusion and Midjourney in interior design education with UTAUT and AHP (survey and expert-weighting methods) on creativity, aesthetics, and feasibility; ratings are of the tools, not scored participant output, and no AI-assistance comparison is described; included in the Ozkan 2026 meta-analysis, so the next stage may want to check the full text.
